look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Geiser's fleabane is a SMALL annual (5–40 cm) with a SLENDER TAPROOT and generally simple herbaceous base. Basal foliage may have 2–4 pairs of teeth or lobes. Lower stem hairs often spread or bend DOWNWARD while upper hairs are straighter/appressed; fresh white-rayed heads have usually 44–70 rays, 3–6 mm long. It is NOT a perennial woody-crown plant like mature E. modestus. Taproot/hair characters are field-key requirements, not fully proved in existing photos.

morphology_keys.stem_hairs: Lower spreading or deflexed; upper strigose
morphology_keys.head: About 44 to 70 rays, 3 to 6 mm long; involucre 2.5 to 3.5 mm high

comparisons.key_distinctions: E. modestus often has woody persistent root crown; E. tenellus has strongly clasping leaves. Former geiseri var. calcicola belongs to E. versicolor.

field_recognition.field_split: Woody perennial crown and old stem bases, often early single head; ray numbers overlap. Root/crown most important.
Clasping cauline leaves and more rays, usually 95–160+; compare actual leaf bases with scale.
Often clasping auriculate stem leaves and many fine rays; examine full plant, not color.

comparisons.caution: Ray and hair characters overlap between fleabanes, and a tiny root feature in photographs cannot certify species identity; no county-native status changes.

crew_field_sequence: Find an intact annual plant with slender taproot; do not infer annual root structure from a flower-only photo.
Check low stem for spreading/deflexed hairs, then upper stem for short straight/appressed hairs using a hand lens.
Check white-rayed heads (typically 44–70 rays, 3–6 mm) and the side of the green involucre with scale.
Compare with E. modestus, which usually has a woody perennial crown; both may have white daisy-like heads.
If the crown or hair transitions are missing, teach 'Erigeron sp.' rather than force a species ID.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Geiser's fleabane — see heads, then check roots
steps: First see a real flowering shoot, narrow leaves and open white-rayed composite heads in the photographs.
Then inspect your own rooted specimen for a slender ANNUAL TAPROOT, not a woody persistent crown.
Use a hand lens for spreading/deflexed hairs low on stem and straighter/appressed hairs above; flower rays overlap other Erigeron.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Annual slender taproot + lower-to-upper hair transition + fresh heads together support Geiser's fleabane. If crown/hairs hidden, use Erigeron sp.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Pressed-photo root area and living daisy heads do NOT show the diagnostic taproot/hairs clearly enough for arrows.
